Lexicon Latīnitātis Cotīdiānae
Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

guilty adjective

of a crime

also found guilty, guilty of, convicted, convict, conviction, be found guilty, convicted of, punish the guilty, convict on many counts of fraud, condemn, conviction (for a crime)

classical

Cic. Rosc. Am. 56
Cic. Off. 2.51: nocentem aliquando, modo nē nefārium impiumque dēfendere

nocēns, nocentis

declension

guilty, culpable

The opposite of innocēns; as a noun, a guilty person.

Other words

  • sōns, sontis — guilty; as a noun, the guilty, offenders

    declension · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 2.18: comprehēnsiō sontium; Traupman 195; Traupman 195: the guilty one; Traupman 324

    As an adjective mostly in the poets; in prose chiefly the noun (Lewis & Short).

  • condemnō, condemnāre, condemnāvī, condemnātum — find guilty, convict

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Rosc. Am. 56: condemnārī nōn potest; Traupman 191, 194; Traupman 194: condemn; Traupman 295

    To be found guilty, condemnārī or damnārī.

  • noxius, noxia, noxium — guilty (of), culpable

    adjective, with the ablative or genitive of the charge, declension · also used · classical · Liv. 39.41: quī citātī nōn affuerant, noxiōs jūdicāvit (Lewis & Short); Traupman 195; Traupman 324

  • manifestus, manifesta, manifestum (+ gen.) — convicted of, caught in

    adjective, with the genitive of the charge, declension · also used · classical · Traupman 296; Sall. J. 35: sceleris manifestus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 194: convicted of

  • condemnātiō, condemnātiōnis f. — a conviction, a condemnation

    noun, third declension · also used · post-classical · Dig. 42.1.59 (Lewis & Short: post-Augustan); Traupman 194; Traupman 296

  • convincō, convincere, convīcī, convictum — convict, prove guilty

    verb with the accusative of the person and the genitive of the charge, conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 296

Examples

  • innocēns, sī accūsātus sit, absolvī potest, nocēns, nisi accūsātus fuerit, condemnārī nōn potest

    an innocent man, if he is accused, can be acquitted; a guilty one cannot be found guilty unless he has been accusedCic. Rosc. Am. 56

  • Estne absolūtus an condemnātus?

    Was he acquitted or found guilty?Traupman 191

  • noxius jūdicārī

    to be found guiltyTraupman 195; cf. Liv. 39.41 (Lewis & Short s.v. noxius)

  • poenam dē sontibus exigere

    to punish the guiltyTraupman 195

  • aliquem multīs crīminibus fraudis convincere

    to convict someone on many counts of fraudTraupman 194

  • in culpā esse

    to be guilty, be at faultTraupman 195

  • Noxius dījūdicātus est.

    He was found guilty.Traupman 324

See also innocent, trial, guilty, crime, criminal.
